# Jarvising

> jarvising (verb, present participle of *jarvis*; also noun): 1. The act of creating innovative projects at scale. 2. Giving people the tools to do it themselves.

jarvising.com is an open portfolio of test projects, experiments and tools built by Jack Stovell (https://jstov.uk/). Each entry shows what it does, how it was made, and how to make your own.

## Entries

- [Entry 001 — Enigma](https://jarvising.com/projects/enigma/): a scroll-driven, fully procedural Three.js teardown of the Enigma I that ends in a faithful, typeable machine (rotors I·II·III, reflector B, ten plug pairs, double-step). The entry page explains what it does, how it was made (one scroll-derived progress value drives every beat; named parts with explode vectors; labels projected from 3D; WebAudio-synthesised sound) and a ten-step recipe for making your own, plus the complete cipher core as code. First shipped 2026-08-27 as jstov.uk lab experiment 008.
- [Entry 001 — live piece](https://jarvising.com/projects/enigma/live/): the teardown itself. Needs WebGL and JavaScript.
- [Entry 002 — Cortex](https://jarvising.com/projects/cortex/): the memory of an AI agent fleet drawn as a living 3D knowledge graph on a holographic "war table", and the open-source React library that draws it, cortex-map (MIT, https://github.com/StovBuilds/cortex-map; not published to npm, so you clone the repository and copy or build packages/cortex-map). The entry page covers what it does, where it comes from (the Jarvis fleet's shared pgvector memory, 3,183 nodes / 3,924 edges verified 2026-07-27 per the public architecture notes), how it was made (fixed deterministic layout on 3d-force-graph, render-on-demand, everything drawn in code) and a seven-step recipe for making your own. First released 2026-07-15. The first entry for sense 2 of the word.
- [Entry 002 — live piece](https://jarvising.com/projects/cortex/live/): the map, over a fictional game studio's second brain (191 nodes, 273 links, 7 clusters; no real data). Needs WebGL and JavaScript; flat 2D on phones.
- [Entry 003 — Inside the Rig](https://jarvising.com/projects/rig/): a scroll-driven Three.js teardown of a flagship-class gaming PC, 17 chapters from inside the processor (an abstract city of logic blocks, then the cache) out through memory, the motherboard, storage, PCIe, the graphics processor, cooling, power and airflow to the whole machine, ending in an exploded, searchable atlas of 104 modelled pieces in eight systems (filters, synonym search, isolate, deep dive, a four-stage explode slider). Parts are modelled at real published dimensions but named generically: no brands, on purpose, enforced in CI. The entry page explains how it was made (an id registry the copy and the builders are both typed against; explode as per-node data; camera keys stamped with scroll progress; a scripted Blender parts library swapped in by id) and an eight-step recipe. First shipped 2026-09-07 as jstov.uk lab page 011.
- [Entry 003 — live piece](https://jarvising.com/projects/rig/live/): the teardown and atlas. Needs WebGL and JavaScript.
- [Entry 004 — Below the Layer](https://jarvising.com/projects/submarine/): a Three.js scene of an early British T-class submarine of the Second World War hunted by a surface escort's ASDIC (active sonar). Dive below the thermocline ("the layer") at 180 ft and the ping bends away, so the echo fades from strong to faint; depth, pressure (gauge psi from depth, 133 psi at the boats' 300 ft rated depth) and echo readouts, an echo trace, and an exploded cutaway of the six compartments. The entry page explains how it was made (a hull lofted from five curves; every material patched to draw the sonar shells, caustics and depth fog; one number for how much of the boat is below the layer) and a seven-step recipe, with history notes and a claim-by-claim sources ledger (docs/submarine-sources.md). Built by Jack Stovell in a conversation with Claude, published as a claude.ai artifact on 2026-09-29, ported here the same day.
- [Entry 004 — live piece](https://jarvising.com/projects/submarine/live/): the submarine scene. Needs WebGL and JavaScript. `?kiosk=1` runs it unattended.

## Pages

- [Home](https://jarvising.com/): the dictionary entry for "jarvising" and the index of entries.

## Source

- [github.com/StovBuilds/jarvising](https://github.com/StovBuilds/jarvising): the whole site, public. Entry 001 lives in `src/enigma/`, entry 002 in `src/cortex/` (the cortex-map source vendored in `src/cortex/lib/`), entry 003 in `src/rig/`, entry 004 in `src/submarine/`.

## Privacy

- The site makes no third-party requests. Analytics are anonymous first-party page counts: no cookies, no IP addresses, no third parties, nothing to consent to. Opt-out switch in the home page footer; Global Privacy Control and Do Not Track are honoured.
